expected.title: Locate the Cavite Event
expected.content:
Our new case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. The NHCP execution-site marker links the later accusation against three priests with this January event.

Keep two places separate: Cavite is linked with the uprising; Bagumbayan in Manila is linked with the later execution. Related events in the same year are not necessarily the same event. This introductory timeline does not settle every disagreement about the causes or extent of the uprising.

Your museum task is to locate the event accurately. We study what happened without acting as fighters.

fields.title: Locate the Event and a Reported Cause
fields.content:
Our case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. Fort San Felipe and the nearby naval arsenal belonged to this setting. An arsenal is a place supplying military equipment and work.

Why were people unhappy? French writer Edmond Plauchut, writing in 1877, connected the uprising with workers losing exemptions from tax and required labor. He described privileges connected with their retirement. An exemption means a person does not have to pay a certain tax or perform a duty. Removing it can change what that person owes. This is a reported cause in his account, not a statement from every worker.

Imagine a classroom example: a rule changes what a person is required to pay. Understanding that change helps explain a complaint. It does not tell us everyone had the same goal. Our next source comparison asks whether the accounts agree about how widely the uprising was planned. Keep Cavite separate from the later execution at Bagumbayan in Manila.

expected.title: Read the Accusation Carefully
expected.content:
After the uprising, colonial authorities accused the priests of involvement. The NHCP marker describes their involvement as alleged. Alleged means claimed, rather than proven merely by saying it. The National Museum describes suspected treason: a charge of acting against the government to which a person owes allegiance.

A caption should distinguish the accusation from proof. A serious punishment does not by itself prove that an accusation was true. Our classroom cards cannot replace examination of historical records.

Repair this fictional label: "They were accused, so they must have organized the mutiny." An accusation and a proven action are different. You are not asked to decide guilt from three short clues.

fields.title: Compare Two Accounts, Then Check the Claim
fields.content:
Read two modern summaries of historical accounts. These are our paraphrases, not quotations.

Account A: Edmond Plauchut wrote in 1877. He linked the uprising with lost tax and required-labor exemptions. He also described mutineers expecting support that did not arrive. A worker complaint and an expectation of support can both appear in an account. Calling his account only a complaint with no plans would leave out that detail.

Account B: Governor Rafael de Izquierdo reported on 31 January 1872. He described the suppression as stopping plans prepared in advance against Spanish rule. This tells us how a colonial official presented the event, not that every accusation in his report is automatically true.

Compare the emphasis: a reported grievance and failed support in A; organized plans in B. A cause is why someone may act. The extent asks how widely action was planned or supported. These are different questions. A wider plan does not by itself prove that Gomes, Burgos and Zamora organized it. Authorities accused the priests, but keep the accusation separate from proof.

Connect the source cards and explain what they support. We do not label either summary the opinion of every French, Spanish or Filipino person.

expected.title: Explain the Whole Case
expected.content:
Your case has three parts. Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication.

The sequence connects events without confusing them. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof. Later remembrance helps explain why the case remained important in concerns about justice and the country.

Complete this report frame silently or with a trusted adult: "The event was ___. The accusation was ___. A later response was ___. It shows ___, but does not prove ___." The quiz checks five lesson topics. If one is difficult, review its scene before targeted practice.

fields.title: Explain Causes, Claims and Responses
fields.content:
Your case now connects a reported cause, an event, a claim and a later response. Plauchut links the uprising with lost exemptions and describes support that did not arrive. Izquierdo presents plans prepared in advance. Their different emphases do not settle who organized the event merely by naming an accused person.

Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof.

Try this report frame: "According to ___, a cause or plan was ___. The other account emphasizes ___. The January event was followed by ___. A later response was ___. Our cards do not prove ___." Use the source names rather than saying all people held one view. Review a difficult topic before targeted practice.
